Subject: Scale priming QA & action items — warm pool + streaming SLOs

Hi Maria / Strato ops team,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum on the SLO qualification work for the payments fraud-detector flow: a concise mutual action plan below.

High-level SLO targets you specified:
- p95 latency <= 220ms for 1kB prompt size (non-streaming)
- streaming first-chunk <= 180ms, subsequent chunk interval <= 200ms
- sustainable throughput: 150 req/s with occasional 2x bursts up to 300 req/s for <5 minutes
- concurrency target: 64 active sessions per model shard

Redwood assumptions & priming approach we proposed:
1) Warm pool: keep N warm workers per shard to meet p95 at burst; engineering recommended N=10 as a starting point for your traffic profile.
2) Scale-up target: cold-to-ready < 35s, ideally < 30s for single-worker allocation during a burst.
3) Queueing: queueing allowed up to 2s for non-critical workflows; for fraud-detect we agreed to prefer warm pool vs queueing.
4) Streaming behavior: prefer continuous KV cache reuse; chunk prefetch enabled to avoid first-chunk penalty.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Strato: provide 48h traffic sample (t+calibrated token sizes) + expected burst cadence — Maria (by 2027-02-16).
- Redwood infra: initial priming checklist + warm pool sizing worksheet — Ben (attached) (by 2027-02-16).
- Redwood engineering: confirm exact kernel/quantization profile that will be used for the test run and expected cold-start delta — Karthik (by 2027-02-15).
- Schedule: propose a 2-hour test window next week to run priming + one controlled burst — Aisha to coordinate (I will send a scheduling poll).

Attachments: stratobank-priming-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with warm-pool calc), slo-matrix-stratobank.pdf (SLO table we reviewed).

Questions for you now that will unblock sizing:
- Is end-to-end call composition single call -> model, or are you chaining multiple models per request?
- For streaming, do you require server-sent events to the client, or are you comfortable with short-poll chunking?

Short note on tradeoffs: increasing warm pool reduces tail latency but increases hourly cost; we'll include cost delta in the worksheet so you can decide (we recommended warm pool for fraud-detect because queueing is risky for time-sensitive alerts).

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite once I hear back on traffic samples.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from the engineering side so expectations are aligned before the run:

1) Warm pool sizing rationale: N=10 was our baseline assuming 8 GPUs with 2 shards each and an average payload of ~1k tokens. If your average prompt is larger than expected the warm pool will need to grow linearly. Please confirm mean token size in the sample.

2) Scale-up timings: our internal measurements show cold-start (container spin + model load) can be 60–90s for full model loads on new nodes; however, for warm pool priming (model already loaded, just worker ready) we typically observe 18–28s. Our goal for this test is to keep the priming path under 30s. During the test we'll capture detailed traces (cold vs primed).

3) Queueing behavior: by default we cap request queueing per worker to 2s — beyond that we open fast-path fallback to a lower-cost model variant or return 429 depending on policy. For Strato we recommend fallback off (i.e., fail-open to preserve deterministic latency) and rely on warm pool sizing instead. Please confirm tradeoff.

4) Streaming specifics: enabling chunk prefetch reduces first-chunk latency but increases memory usage per worker by ~6%; we can run with chunk prefetch enabled for the test window.

I'll attach the short tech checklist with the exact runtime flags we'll enable. If you want, I can also include a small script to replay the traffic sample against our staging cluster.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
